title: Why do things float or sink?
examples: Teacher, why does a big rock sink but a big log float?
What makes something float in water?
Can you explain upthrust to me?

explain.say: Today we learn why things float or sink in water.

draw.text: Why do things float or sink?

explain.say: First we look at density. Density is how much stuff is packed into a space.
Next is upthrust. Upthrust is the upward push the liquid gives to an object.
An object floats when the upthrust is bigger than its weight.
If the weight is bigger than the upthrust, the object will sink down.
Ships float because they push a lot of water aside, making upthrust large.

faq.q: Why does a big rock sink but a big log float?
faq.a: The rock is very dense, so its weight pulls it down more than the water can push up.
asks: What is the difference between density and weight?
Why does density matter when floating?

faq.q: Does the size of something decide if it floats?
faq.a: No, it is the density of the object that really decides if it floats or sinks.
asks: Is it just about being big enough?
Does volume change the floating ability?

faq.a: Upthrust is the upward force that the water pushes up on the submerged object.
asks: Where does the upward push come from?
Is upthrust the same as buoyancy?

faq.q: Why do ships float if they are made of steel?
faq.a: Ships are shaped to push enough water aside that the upthrust balances their weight.
asks: How does the shape help it float?

faq.q: Does the water need to be salty or fresh?
faq.a: The density of the water affects the upthrust, so saltier water can sometimes support more weight.
asks: Is fresh water different from sea water?

facts: Density is calculated by dividing mass by volume.
Upthrust is the upward force exerted by the fluid.
Objects float when the upthrust equals the weight.
Ships float by displacing a volume of water equal to their weight.

quiz.say: A small piece of wood floats because its density is:
quiz.why: Wood is less dense than water, so the upthrust is greater than its weight.

wrong.0: While temperature affects water, density is the main factor here.
wrong.2: This would mean the object is very heavy and would sink.
wrong.3: If it were equal, it would float, but this is not the main reason.

quiz.say: If an object sinks, it means:

options.show: its weight is greater than the upthrust
options.say: its weight is greater than the upthrust

options.show: the water pressure is too high
options.say: the water pressure is too high

quiz.why: When weight pulls down more than the water pushes up, the object sinks.

wrong.1: Low density usually causes floating, not sinking.
wrong.2: Water pressure causes upthrust, which is what we compare to weight.
wrong.3: Many things made of metal can float if shaped correctly.

quiz.say: When a ship floats, it uses which principle?
quiz.why: The ship must push aside a weight of water equal to its own weight.

wrong.0: Mass is important, but the way it displaces water is the key concept.
wrong.1: Strength keeps it together, but displacement keeps it afloat.
wrong.2: Surface area is part of it, but displacement is the scientific rule.
